Content: Naglingkud lang siya didtu ug walà magtingug,
He just sat there without saying anything.
He’s just a houseboy, but he wants to have the say.
Walà ku muanhi arun lang kasab-an,
I didn’t come here merely to get a scolding.
All she could do was cry. (Lit. She was merely up to crying.)
My sufferings were all in vain (nothing more than vain).
This is cheap because it is only a peso.
with commands or exhortation: just do [so-and-so]—it’s a small thing to do.
Maglakaw lang ta, duul ra man,
Let’s just walk. It’s not far.
please [do], it’s just a little favor to ask.
Come on. Please, let me do it.
with negatives: not bother to do.
Dì lang ta mangatúlug rung gabíi,
Let’s not bother going to sleep this evening.
Dì lang ang inahan kun dì hasta anak maapiktahan,
Not only the mother but also the child will be affected.
just so it happens, though it isn’t desirable.
Iwarì lang nà. Basta lang mawálà sa ákung panan-aw,
Get rid of it. Just so it gets out of my sight.
just now, just recently, just yesterday.
just do at [such-and-such time] (and no other time).
They just collect garbage on Thursdays.
gee, I don’t know (I’m only up to saying I don’t know).
I’ll sell it to whoever is first.
Maáyu untà, gáling lang nasayup ang miskla,
It should have been good, only the mixture was in the wrong proportions.
just, take [so-and-so] rather than some other choice.
with nominal predicate and verb subject: let [so-and-so] do it.
You ask. (Lit. let you be the one to ask.)
If you do it, you take the responsibility.
with quantities: just make it [so-and-so] much.
Can I have it for thirty?
with verb: take the choice of [do]ing.
Ang isdang dílì mahálin gamsun lang, dílì bularun,
If they can’t sell the fish, they just salt it. They don’t dry it.
Ayaw lag anhi ugmà, kay mahímu man sa Huybis,
Don’t bother coming tomorrow because you can do it on Thursday.
well, all right, I’ll agree to it.
Sígi lang. Dì lang ku mudayug palit kay mahal,
Never mind. I won’t buy it because it’s expensive.
Sígi lang, itúgut ku na lang nig bayinti,
Oh, all right. I’ll let you have it for twenty centavos.
just let me (him) have it rather than s.o. else.
ákù lang ni. Kadtu lay ihátag ni Pidru,
Let me have this one. Just let Pedro have the other one.
Mahadluk lang ta bisan sa pagpanimátì lang,
We can’t help getting cold shivers, even just hearing about it.

2c4a it cannot be otherwise. ‘Mu ba siya ang nakaingun?’—‘Mu lang!’ ‘Is he the one that caused it?’—‘Of course! Who else could it have been.’2c4b yes, most certainly so. ‘Mukáun kag surbíti?’—‘Káun mu lang,’ ‘Would you like to eat ice cream?’—‘I sure would.’
now it is only [so-and-so much] where it was more before.
Sukad sila namalhin aku na lang ang nahibilin,
After they moved away I was the only one left.
Human na ang tanan, paglimpiyu na lang,
Everything is done. Only the cleaning remains.
Duul na lang ang átung gidulngan,
It is just a little way further to where we’re going.
just take [so-and-so] rather than some other manifestly better choice.
with nominal predicate and verb subject: [so-and-so] will do it, though it should not be so.
Aku na lay tiwas áni, kay madúgay ug láing táwu,
Let me just do this myself because it would take forever if s.o. else were to do it.
with quantities: just make it [so-and-so much] (which is less than what one would ordinarily get).
Just let me have it for thirty, this time, all right? 3b2a
just here (when I really want to do it elsewhere).
Kay lisud man ug musúd, anhi na lang ku sa iskína manáug,
Since it’s difficult to take a vehicle in, I’ll just get off at the corner.
[do] as the best choice under the circumstances.
Gamsa na lang nang isdáa kay wà nay mupalit,
You might as well just salt that fish because there isn’t anybody who’ll buy it.
Ayaw na lag dad-a ug bug-atan ka,
Don’t bother taking it if you find it too heavy.
let me (him) have it (although you might have s.t. better to do with it).
Let me have it, may I?
I thank you, since I can’t pay you any other way.
Ug dì ka pabáyad, salámat na lang,
Since you won’t let me pay you, just let me thank you.
Sa tantung kapungut nalímut na lang siya sa íyang kaugalíngun,
He was so angry he just forgot himself.
following expressions referring to time: it’s already [so-and-so] late and s.t. still hasn’t happened or hasn’t stopped happening.
Udtu na lang ug naglúkun lang gihápun sa banig,
It’s already noon, and he’s still curled up asleep.
Gabíi na lang wà gihápun siya,
It’s already night and he still has not come home.
obviously, can’t help being that way.
Kláru na lang nga muhílak ug ímung kusiun,
Obviously he’s going to cry if you pinch him.
Malumus untà ku. Salámat na lang nga dinhay nakakità nákù,
I would have drowned, but thank God, s.o. saw me.
Karun pa lang ku makakità sa ingun,
This is the very first time I ever saw anything like that.
if it was so at [such-and-such] a time already, it would be even worse later.
Sa súgud pa lang nahanákan na siya,
At the very beginning he was already out of breath.
Dì ku mudúul sa irù kay paákun pa lang ku,
I won’t go near the dog, because I might get bitten.
Dì pa lang ka amígu nákù, ikíha ta ka,
If you were not my friend, I would have filed a case against you.
Aku pa lay gipabúhat, gwápu tag ági,
if they had told me to do it, it would have come out nice.
